stories.headline: Bundesrat unexpectedly blocks government's 1,000-euro energy relief bonus; coalition scrambles for alternatives
stories.summary: Germany's upper house rejected the Merz government's flagship 1,000-euro tax-free employee bonus designed to offset Iran-war energy price increases, dealing a significant political blow to Chancellor Merz and Finance Minister Klingbeil. The coalition announced a summit for Tuesday to search for alternative relief measures, with Söder declaring the premium definitively dead and Bundesrat opposition citing cost-shifting to states and municipalities.

stories.headline: Germany revives Tomahawk cruise missile purchase bid; Pistorius plans Washington trip after US cancels deployment
stories.summary: The Financial Times reported that Germany is reviving its bid to purchase Tomahawk cruise missiles directly from the US after Washington cancelled plans to station the weapons on German soil. Defense Minister Pistorius is planning a trip to Washington to push the purchase, contingent on securing a meeting with Defense Secretary Hegseth; Pistorius had previously warned the Tomahawk cancellation created a 'capability gap' more serious than the troop withdrawal. Foreign Minister Wadephul also confirmed ongoing talks with the US.

stories.headline: Trump withdraws 5,000 US troops from Germany amid Iran-war NATO tensions; Germany responds with calm
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced the withdrawal of approximately 5,000 of the roughly 39,000 US troops stationed in Germany, including the 2nd Stryker Cavalry Regiment at Vilseck. Defense Minister Pistorius called the move expected but played it down in terms of deterrence impact, while Chancellor Merz stated NATO strength depends on shared goals rather than troop numbers alone. The withdrawal is framed by US officials as retaliation for Merz's comments on the Iran war.

stories.headline: Merz government reaches historic approval lows after one year; AfD leads polls for first time
stories.summary: On the one-year anniversary of the Merz government, multiple polls showed record dissatisfaction: the ARD Deutschlandtrend recorded 84-86% disapproval of the government and only 16% satisfaction with Merz personally — the lowest for any post-war chancellor at this stage. Simultaneously, the AfD overtook the CDU/CSU in multiple polls, leading with 27-28% versus Union at 23-24%, and half of respondents expected the coalition to collapse before its term ends.

stories.headline: Bundeswehr musterungszentren announced and conscription reform implementation begins; 28% of young men ignore questionnaire
stories.summary: The Defense Ministry announced 24 locations nationwide for new military screening centers to be operational by mid-2027, as implementation of the January 2026 conscription reform accelerates. Of roughly 206,000 young men who received questionnaires, 28% have not responded despite a legal obligation; the ministry threatened fines of up to 1,000 euros. Pistorius also committed to presenting parliament a Bundeswehr capability report by July 31.

stories.headline: Wadephul proposes scrapping EU unanimity principle in keynote speech; pushback from Eastern members
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Wadephul delivered a keynote address at the Konrad Adenauer Foundation outlining a six-point plan to reform the EU, centered on replacing the unanimity principle in foreign and security policy with qualified majority voting. The proposal drew support from twelve member states but resistance from Czech Foreign Minister Macinka and others, who rejected 'abstract visions from Brussels.' Wadephul cited Hungarian obstruction of Ukraine aid as the key argument for reform.

stories.headline: Steinmeier visits Sweden and Finland on defense resilience tour; calls for US reliability in NATO
stories.summary: Federal President Steinmeier made a two-day visit to Stockholm and Helsinki, touring military bases, civil defense bunkers, and meeting with leaders including Finnish President Stubb and the Swedish royal family. He praised the Nordic model of societal resilience, called for US reliability within NATO amid troop withdrawal fears, and renewed his proposal for a social service obligation in Germany. Multiple articles discussed lessons Germany could draw from Finland's total defense model.

stories.headline: Tax revenue forecast cut by €87.5 billion through 2030 due to Iran war; budget pressure intensifies
stories.summary: Germany's independent tax expert council released a significantly downgraded five-year revenue forecast, projecting €87.5 billion less than the autumn 2026 baseline through 2030, attributing the shortfall primarily to the economic impact of the Iran war and related energy price spikes. Finance Minister Klingbeil confirmed the figures while blaming the war; the DIW called it a warning signal as inflation hit 2.9% in April.

stories.headline: Putin proposes ex-Chancellor Schroeder as Ukraine peace mediator; Germany dismisses proposal
stories.summary: Russian President Putin publicly proposed former Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder as a mediator in Ukraine peace talks, citing their personal relationship. Berlin dismissed the proposal as not credible, noting Russia had changed none of its conditions, and SPD officials distanced themselves from Schroeder given his longstanding ties to the Russian energy sector.

stories.headline: Merz government plans to abolish daily 8-hour cap in favor of weekly working hours limit; unions threaten mass protests
stories.summary: The Merz government confirmed plans to reform Germany's working time law by replacing the daily 8-hour maximum with a weekly cap, which critics say could allow working days of up to 13 hours. Labor Minister Bas was tasked to present a draft law in June. Trade unions at the DGB congress threatened mass protests in June, calling the reform a 'health accelerant.'

stories.headline: Baden-Württemberg CDU-Grüne coalition ratified by party congresses; Özdemir set to become Minister-President
stories.summary: Both the CDU and Grüne party congresses in Baden-Württemberg voted to approve the coalition agreement two months after the March state election, paving the way for Cem Özdemir (Grüne) to become Minister-President. CDU leader Hagel will serve as Interior Minister and Deputy PM; the surprise personnel announcement was CDU federal politician Andreas Jung as Education Minister.

stories.headline: AfD polls at 41% in Sachsen-Anhalt ahead of September election; absolute majority scenario discussed
stories.summary: A new poll commissioned by MDR, Mitteldeutsche Zeitung, and Volksstimme showed the AfD at 41% in Sachsen-Anhalt, where a state election is due in September, with CDU at 26%. Analysts discussed whether a CDU-led minority government or a difficult multi-party coalition could block an AfD majority. CDU Ministerpräsident Schulze trails AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund in direct comparison.
